properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 16 at 12:20AM ChST until September 16 at 3:15AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Guam...

* WHEN...Until 315 AM ChST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1220 AM ChST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Up to 0.2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dededo, Tamuning, Yigo, Mangilao, Chalan Pago-Ordot, Barrigada,
Yona, Hagatna Heights, Andersen AFB, Talofofo,
Mongmong-Toto-Maite, Sinajana, Inarajan, Asan, Merizo, Piti,
Santa Rita and Umatac.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
properties.area: Guam, GU

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued September 15 at 10:07AM EDT until September 15 at 10:45AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
SMWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA out 60 NM...

* Until 1045 AM EDT.

* At 1007 AM EDT, showers producing waterspouts were located along a
line from near Beaufort 45 Feet Reef to 8 NM south of Betsy Ross
Reef, moving southwest at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported. At 1003 AM, Hilton Head
Emergency Management relayed a video of a large waterspout
just offshore of Hilton Head. While this waterspout has
dissipated, additional waterspouts are possible.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can create locally hazardous seas.

* Locations impacted include...
Hilton Head Reef, Beaufort 45 Feet Reef, General Gordon, Betsy Ross
Reef, Gaskins Bank Wreck, Gaskin Banks, Fish America, Whitewater
Reef and Calibogue Sound.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
properties.area: Coastal waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA out 20 NM; Waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA extending from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued September 15 at 11:45PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
The areas affected include...western  Guam Coastal Waters...western
Rota Coastal Waters...

At 1145 PM ChST, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This thunderstorm was
located over the western coastal waters of Rota, moving southwest
around 25 knots toward the western coastal waters of Guam.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.
properties.area: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters; Tinian Coastal Waters

properties.title: Flood Watch issued September 15 at 8:08AM CDT until September 15 at 4:00PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in Iowa...

East Nishnabotna River near Atlantic affecting Cass County.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...East Nishnabotna River near Atlantic, or from Troublesome
Creek near Atlantic to Indian Creek near Lewis.

* WHEN...From this morning to this afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 11.5 feet, and rising.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached based on the latest
forecast information.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

River forecasts include observed precipitation plus forecast
precipitation over the next 24 hours.
properties.area: Cass

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 9:25PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Elevated water levels are expected along the river over the next
several days due to recent heavy rainfall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue rising to 28.2 feet just
after midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.4
feet on 08/05/2024.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.
properties.area: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 9:23PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Monday the stage was 9.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Wednesday morning and continue rising to 12.4 feet Thursday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.5
feet on 08/31/2002.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.
